source.title: Using Mechanistic Interpretability to Craft Adversarial Attacks against Large Language Models
source.authors: Thomas Winninger; B. Addad; Katarzyna Kapusta

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates a known SAE latent by optimizing inputs to activate it and reporting the resulting token sequences. This is indirect evidence about semantic content in an LLM SAE feature, but it does not test the original toy-model superposition method.
record.gate_note: The paper's central SSR jailbreak success rates, refusal-direction analyses, and cross-layer results do not test the superposition or capacity claims. The SAE result is included because it reports what a selected feature responds to. The SAE latent was already identified in prior work; this paper does not test whether an SAE recovers it from model activations.
record.test_reason: A jailbreak paper. Its only SAE result takes a latent already labelled 'firearms' in a published GPT2-small SAE and uses it to demo the reverse-lens method. The reported quantity, about one interpretable run in five, measures how well the method works. The paper does not measure whether features are superposed, whether SAEs recover sparse features, or how prevalent or stable such features are. The refusal-direction, probe and ASR results concern safety representations, not superposition.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the main conclusion is about attacks. The authors conclude that SSR achieves 80-95% jailbreak success on Gemma2, Llama3.2 and Qwen2.5 in seconds to minutes. They argue this shows mechanistic interpretability can beat traditional baselines such as GCG. They also suggest SSR and the reverse-lens could become minor interpretability tools. The SAE reverse-lens result is a single preliminary demonstration on one known latent.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not reproduce or test the toy-model superposition method; it studies refusal mechanisms and uses SSR, including a reverse-lens procedure for a selected SAE latent.
record.method_sensitivity: For the SAE reverse-lens experiment, the result concerns one selected feature in one model; the authors report that interpretable outcomes were not consistent across runs.
record.problems: The SAE evidence is preliminary and limited to one preselected latent in GPT2-small. The paper does not test SAE recovery, feature prevalence, or feature stability.
record.rows_left_out: SSR jailbreak attack success rates, steering comparisons, probe accuracies, and refusal-direction geometry were omitted because they do not measure the claim versions about superposition, capacity, or SAE recovery.

untested.parts: Toy-model superposition, geometry and sparsity transition: not studied.
Capacity account of polysemanticity: not studied.
Polysemanticity without capacity pressure: not studied.
Whether LLM features are spread across neurons, or whether SAEs recover sparse features from activations: not tested. A pre-existing latent is used as a target only.
Completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features: not studied.
Whether superposed features are 1-D or multi-dimensional: not studied. The paper assumes a single linear refusal direction, following prior work.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' guess and both V4 labels are dropped. Confirming a known latent's firearms association with an input-optimisation method does not bear on whether SAEs recover sparse features or on superposition. The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition only in related work.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, feature overlap and geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions.
Capacity pressure, neuron polysemanticity, and allocation of dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.

The paper tests the semantic association of one previously identified SAE latent, not whether SAEs recover sparse features from model activations, how prevalent such features are, or whether the result generalizes.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Whether features involved in superposition are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Optimized inputs to maximize activation of a selected SAE latent using the reverse-lens procedure.

conditions.value: previously identified as responding to firearms-related tokens

rows.measure: Semantic content of generated input sequences; frequency of interpretable results
rows.value: Generated sequences included terms such as “handguns,” “weapon,” and “gun”; interpretable results occurred in approximately one in five runs.
rows.note: The paper describes this as a preliminary result. The latent was selected because prior work had identified its firearms association; this result supports that association but does not establish SAE feature recovery.
rows.check: Measures the reverse-lens method's success at finding inputs for one preselected, previously characterised SAE latent (GPT2-small attn L9, latent 20668). The 1-in-5 rate is the method's success rate, not a measure of SAE feature recovery, sparsity or superposition. It is a method-performance and selection result, so it should not be linked to V4.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
